task.description: Security gate for REQ-037's implementation. Read docs/agents/instructions/security-invariants.md first, then git diff origin/main...HEAD -- lib/letflow/definitions/promotion_review_store.ex lib/letflow/definitions/promotion.ex. IMPORTANT DIFFERENCE FROM REQ-036: unlike REQ-036's 3 modules (all read-only), promote_definition/3 in promotion.ex PERFORMS WRITES -- it deprecates the current ACTIVE process_definitions row and activates a target row, inside a transaction, then appends an event. This means security-invariants.md's write-time tenant_id derivation rule (the 2026-08-17 addendum referenced in REQ-036's own design doc footnote as 'does not apply since all 3 modules are read-only') DOES apply here and must be checked properly -- confirm every write derives tenant_id/schema correctly and cannot be influenced by unvalidated caller input. Also check: (a) promotion_review_store.ex's row_version-guarded UPDATE pattern for the 6 state-transition functions -- confirm no function allows a caller to bypass the tenant-scoping (:prefix) that scopes promotion_reviews rows; (b) approve_review/4's digest-mismatch check actually prevents an attacker from approving a review against a plan they didn't see (calls PromotionDigest.verify_digest/2 correctly); (c) promote_definition/3's permission_checker/tenant_classifier reuse from PromotionPlan -- confirm it's genuinely the same fail-closed pattern (Keyword.fetch!, no default) as REQ-036's already-approved implementation, not a weakened copy.
acceptance_criteria: Scope test: confirm this diff touches a tenant-data path (promotion_reviews read/write, process_definitions write, cross-tenant read) -- expected: YES
For each of INV-1..INV-8, determine APPLIES or NOT-APPLICABLE against this diff, and run the 'How to verify' check for each APPLIES invariant

Specifically confirm the write-time tenant_id/prefix derivation rule (2026-08-17 addendum) is satisfied for promote_definition/3's writes -- this is the first write path across REQ-036/REQ-037's combined diff
Confirm promotion_review_store.ex's 6 transition functions cannot cross tenant boundaries via a caller-supplied review_id belonging to a different tenant's :prefix
Confirm permission_checker/tenant_classifier reuse in promote_definition/3 is genuinely fail-closed, not weakened relative to REQ-036's already-reviewed implementation
FAIL immediately on any applicable invariant failing -- all BLOCKER, no partial credit
